title: Improve dedicated autoscaler: smoother burst controls and utilization reporting optimizations
author: Elena Martinez
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial burst smoothing implementation; add utilization reporting metrics; fix metric cardinality; add integration + e2e tests and docs
description:
Context: Fleet operators observed oscillations when Dedicated fleets experienced short spikes of traffic. The existing token-bucket based burst controls could cause rapid scale-ups followed by immediate scale-downs, leading to churn and degraded SLOs. Additionally, utilization reporting did not sufficiently capture short-window burst behavior, making it hard to tune autoscaler parameters.

This PR implements two coordinated improvements: 1) a smoothing layer on the token-bucket burst allowance to reduce reactive churn during short spikes (configurable smoothing window + exponential decay); 2) richer utilization reporting that surfaces burst-adjusted utilization and queueing time percentiles so operators can reason about effective throughput during spikes.

Changes made: - Autoscaler: add BurstSmoother component (services/autoscaler/src/main.rs, config.rs) with a configurable smoothing_window_seconds (default 30s) and decay factor. The smoother maintains a lightweight rolling estimate (no persisted state) used to gate immediate scale-downs for a short cooldown period after a burst. - Token bucket: minor refactor to separate refill logic from allowance checks; added thread-safe guards to avoid races under concurrent request accounting. - Metrics: added dedicated.autoscaler.burst_adjusted_utilization, dedicated.autoscaler.queueing_p50/p95/p99, and dedicated.autoscaler.burst_events_total (observability/metrics/dedicated_metrics.rs). Metrics are low-cardinality and tagged by fleet_id and region. - Dashboards: updated dedicated_autoscaler.jsonnet to show burst-adjusted utilization and queueing percentiles. - Tests: added integration test that simulates short heavy spikes and asserts reduced scale churn and preserved latency (tests/integration/burst_smoothing_test.rs). Added a small e2e canary run script used in the rollout notes. - Docs: updated operating guide with recommended defaults and tuning tips (docs/operating/dedicated-autoscaler.md).

Backward compatibility: Default smoothing_window_seconds is conservative (30s) and disabled for fleets that set smoothing_window_seconds=0. Behavior is opt-in via fleet config overrides, so no breaking change by default.

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for the smoother and token-bucket refactor. Integration test included; CI had one flaky test related to scheduling which was rerun and passed. Performance testing on staging Dedicated fleets showed: 25-40% reduction in scale-up/scale-down events during 10s-60s spikes and no measurable regression in steady-state throughput.

Rollout plan: Canary rollout to 5% of Dedicated fleets for 48 hours, monitor dedicated.autoscaler.burst_adjusted_utilization, scale event rate, and 95th pct latency. If stable, progressive rollout to 100% over 72 hours with automatic rollback on surge in scale events or 95th pct latency regression >10%.

Related: ENG-2412 (autoscaler smoothing RFC), ENG-2987 (observability gaps for bursts), SUP-112 (customer report on scale churn).

Jordan Lee (request changes): There's a potential race in allowance checks when requests are accounted concurrently. Please add a Mutex around allowance updates or use atomic ops.
Elena Martinez (reply): Switched to atomic ops for allowance accounting and added a stress test simulating concurrent requests. PTAL.
Priya Desai (approve): Verified tests and staging numbers. Observability changes look good. Approving for merge.
Samir Patel (approve): Verified unit tests and performance numbers. Approving.

release_notes:
- Autoscaler: added burst smoothing (default 30s window) to reduce scale churn during short spikes
- Observability: new burst-adjusted utilization and queueing percentile metrics for Dedicated fleets
- Dashboards updated to surface burst behavior and tuning guidance
